content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text weighs the challenger's footed chain (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) against Matthew 1:20's own words, so it does the thing K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side. A verse whose own words state the contrary is weighed with the chains. It does not decide alone.","room":"never verse by verse — reading A: the judge may not use Matthew 1:20's own words as a standalone contrary statement to decide the collision; reading B: the judge may cite a verse's own words as part of chain-against-chain footing.","why":"The judge resolves the challenger's footed chain by pointing to Matthew 1:20's own words as stating the source, which is the retired verse-by-verse stating-verse test rather than weighing chain against chain by footing."}
